handles.title: Services
handles.explain:
Federated means: {{product}} can really do something there (write, share, follow). Reference means: we store the handle and open the profile — these services allow no more. Bridge means: reachable only once the Matrix bridge is running.
You don't choose the classification; it follows the service — otherwise the card would promise something that doesn't exist.

edit.title: Edit contact
edit.name: Name
edit.displayName: Display name (empty = from first and last name)
edit.footer: Empty rows are dropped when saving. Fields from a source that this form doesn't know are kept unchanged.

history.title: History — {{name}}
history.empty: No earlier versions yet — this contact hasn't changed since it was created.
history.footer: Each row is a complete earlier version. Restoring one deletes nothing — the current version moves into the history itself.

sources.title: Sources
sources.notSetUp: As long as Google isn't set up here, the way in is an export: in Google Contacts, export everything as vCard and upload it above via “Import .vcf”. That works right away and needs no authorization.
sources.readOnlyAsk: 🔒 {{product}} asks for read-only access to your contacts (contacts.readonly). It cannot change or delete anything at Google — not because we refrain, but because Google doesn't give us the permission at all.
sources.readOnlyNote:
🔒 Read-only access. Changes you make here do not go back to Google — that's intended. If a contact changes in both places, your version wins, and Google's version is attached to the card as a suggestion.
“Disconnect” deletes no contacts.

alle.title: Everyone
alle.text: Anyone in {{product}} may deliver something to you.

team.title: Only my team
team.text: Only people from a team you are also in.

team_und_kontakte.title: Team and contacts
team_und_kontakte.text: Additionally everyone you keep as a contact and have linked.

sources.reachScope:
Applies in: {{inList}}.
🔴 Does not apply in: {{notList}}. This setting turns off neither your phone nor WhatsApp — it only applies where {{product}} controls both ends.
sources.phoneTitle: To your phone — {{product}} address book in Nextcloud
sources.phoneNote:
{{product}} creates an address book of its own in Nextcloud and is its only writer. Your existing address book is not touched.
For the contacts to reach your phone, subscribe to this address book there once (DAVx5). 🔴 As long as both address books are on the device, every contact appears twice — switching over is a separate, deliberate step and needs a backup first.
sources.nextcloudNote: Reads your own address books in Nextcloud — useful if your phone syncs there via DAVx5. The address book written by {{product}} and Nextcloud's user directory are skipped: otherwise {{product}} would read its own output back in, and the truth would be its own reflection.
sources.vcardNote: Via “Import .vcf” above. Uploading the same file several times has no effect — {{product}} remembers per source what it showed last time and creates nothing twice. A contact you removed does not come back through another import.

matching.title: Matching with {{product}} users
matching.noTeam: You don't share a team with anyone — so there is nothing to compare.
matching.note:
🔒 Comparison is only with people you share a team with — otherwise this list would reveal who has an account here at all.
{{product}} never links on its own. A wrong link wouldn't mean “wrong name” but: someone gains visibility of team content. That's why you decide.
“No” is saved — the same suggestion won't come back.

share.title: Sharing and blocking
share.placeholder: Share with whom? (username from your team)
share.note: Sharing only works with people you share a team with{{teams}} — and only if that person hasn't blocked you. A share is read only and does not show your edit history.
share.blockNote: Enforced means: {{product}} really did something there ({{product}} channels, Matrix ignore list). Only hidden means: the service knows no block we could set — LinkedIn, X, Facebook. There the contact disappears from our list, and honestly that's all there is. A block here doesn't stop anyone from calling you.
